definition: Finding an integral by recognising the integrand as the derivative of a known function, often by reversing the chain rule, then differentiating the guess to check it and fix any constant factor.

Finding $\int f(g(x))\,g'(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$ by letting $u = g(x)$, so that $g'(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$ becomes $\mathrm{d}u$, integrating with respect to $u$ and writing the answer in terms of $x$ again; for a definite integral, you can change the limits to values of $u$ instead of writing $x$ back.
